incidents.victim: Financial institutions, Southeast Asia and global
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — Cambodia-based financially motivated intrusion group
incidents.vector: An agentic AI offensive framework ("ARTEX") combined with conventional tools to exploit anonymous file-upload and server-side request forgery flaws, then deploy open-source remote access trojans.
incidents.impact: Ongoing credential theft, lateral movement, and data exfiltration at machine speed against financial organizations, primarily in Southeast Asia with some large global targets.

incidents.victim: Multiple companies (UK fintech, US hospitals, mutual fund firm, investment firm, bank, pet food company)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — wire fraud and deepfake impersonation ring
incidents.vector: AI-generated deepfake audio and video impersonating company CEOs and law-firm attorneys, paired with fake e-signature and NDA lures, tricked accounting staff into authorizing large wire transfers.
incidents.impact: At least $129 million stolen from thousands of targeted victims between July 2024 and February 2026; three men charged by the Justice Department, two already arrested in Spain and the UK.

incidents.victim: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
incidents.vector: Not disclosed; theft was traced via blockchain analysis after stolen funds began moving through laundering channels.
incidents.impact: $133 million stolen from the French banking group's cryptocurrency reserve, discovered by an independent blockchain investigator.

incidents.victim: Norad (Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation)
incidents.vector: Attackers gained network access through 27 compromised accounts.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to more than 20,000 grant applicants was stolen; Norad is investigating with Norway's National Security Authority.

incidents.victim: Executive Office of the President (White House network)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — commercial residential-proxy network operators
incidents.vector: White House staffer devices had residential-proxy apps bundled inside free mobile and desktop software, silently renting out the government's IP addresses to third-party customers.
incidents.impact: At least 28 separate proxy services, including a Russian-founded provider, were found exiting through White House network address space 236 times over a 30-day window, exposing government IPs to anonymized third-party traffic.

incidents.victim: US financial system and ransomware/scam-extortion victims laundered through MEXC Global
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — cryptocurrency exchange facilitating ransomware and sanctions-evasion payments
incidents.vector: Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC Global failed to implement anti-money-laundering controls, allowing it to process ransomware extortion payments, scam proceeds, and transactions with sanctioned entities including Russia's Garantex/Grinex and Iran's IRGC-Qods Force.
incidents.impact: Treasury's FinCEN order under Operation Economic Outcast cut MEXC Global off from the US financial system after finding the exchange facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit transactions from 2021-2026, including roughly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and ransomware/scam payment flows.

incidents.victim: Chainalysis and its customers
incidents.vector: Attacker used agentic AI-driven techniques to gain unauthorized access to internal systems and tools, including an on-path attack that intercepted some customer password traffic.
incidents.impact: Names, usernames, password hashes, and live authentication tokens for all Chainalysis users were exposed; some Know Your Transaction customer accounts were accessed, forcing multiple products offline.

incidents.victim: Organizations and individuals in Ukraine, US, and Europe
incidents.vector: Watering-hole compromise of legitimate websites, lookalike domains, and a supply-chain compromise of Ukrainian analytics provider Plerdy delivered device-fingerprinting code and exploit chains to unpatched iOS and Android devices.
incidents.impact: Browser cookies, messages, passwords, contacts, photos, and other sensitive data were stolen from thousands of potentially exposed mobile users, concentrated in Ukraine.

incidents.victim: US and global victims of Prince Group-run scam-compound fraud networks
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — transnational scam-compound operation (Prince Group)
incidents.vector: Southeast Asia-based scam compounds run by the Prince Group Transnational Criminal Organization used digital-asset investment scams and romance scams to defraud victims, laundering proceeds through offshore shell companies; a separate Malaysian individual was sanctioned for running Africa-based scam operations.
incidents.impact: OFAC sanctioned 4 individuals and 41 entities (plus one additional designee under the cyber-focused Executive Order 13694) as a follow-on to prior 2025/2026 designations, targeting a network tied to billions of dollars in losses to American victims.

incidents.victim: Queens Public Library
incidents.vector: Ransomware encrypted library systems; initial access method not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: Wi-Fi, on-site computers, checkout machines, digital media services, and the mobile app were taken down across 66 branches serving 2.3 million residents.

incidents.victim: The Kyiv Independent
incidents.vector: Hackers breached the news outlet's content management system.
incidents.impact: Attackers sent a newsletter to subscribers containing fake news, including false claims that Ukraine's president had been shot or had launched a nuclear strike on Kyiv.

incidents.victim: Owners of 1.3M+ Android TV boxes and other IoT devices globally
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ad-fraud and residential-proxy botnet operator
incidents.vector: A device manufacturer allegedly pre-loaded backdoor malware onto Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT products at the point of manufacture, enrolling them into a botnet.
incidents.impact: A 1.3 million-device botnet used for ad fraud and residential-proxy resale was dismantled by Google and industry partners; access to 10 million additional compromised systems was severed.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian manufacturing company (transportation sector)
incidents.vector: Destructive data-wiping malware deployed against IT systems.
incidents.impact: First-ever destructive wiper attack attributed to Belarusian state-linked hackers, disrupting systems at a Ukrainian manufacturer with an important transportation-sector role.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric-vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers took over master user accounts for Li Auto smart EVs, many registered via a Chinese eSIM provider, then locked out legitimate owners.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners were locked out of their vehicles and extorted to regain access; the true number of affected vehicles is believed to be higher.

incidents.victim: European supermarket chains and French Blood Establishment blood banks
incidents.attacker: Unknown — pro-Russia hacktivist groups claimed credit (unverified)
incidents.vector: Internet-exposed refrigeration controllers (Danfoss, Dixell, Copeland XWEB), many using default credentials, were remotely reconfigured into continuous defrost/heating cycles.
incidents.impact: About 700 French supermarkets were hit Oct 11-12; a second wave Nov 1-2 struck 100-115 retail locations across 10+ more European countries. Units reached up to 50°C, spoiling food and starting some fires; Ahold Delhaize separately estimates up to €250M in losses. French national blood bank refrigeration was also targeted but no plasma was spoiled, prompting a joint CISA/FBI/HHS/USDA/DOT advisory.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency platforms Flap, Kintsu, Pickle Finance, Origami Finance
incidents.vector: Attacker compromised a customer-support account at domain registrar Name.com and used it to redirect 15 cryptocurrency-related domains to phishing sites.
incidents.impact: Customer wallets were drained across multiple affected cryptocurrency platforms.

incidents.victim: Chainstack (blockchain hosting platform) and its customers
incidents.attacker: Unknown — used AI tools to automate the intrusion
incidents.vector: Attackers used AI tools to speed up and automate a breach of blockchain hosting platform Chainstack, gaining unauthorized access to internal systems.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen from Chainstack in an incident that took place in late October 2026.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: A multi-stage social engineering campaign combined a trojanized Homebrew install with a fake multi-round job interview and malicious coding test to compromise engineers' devices, then used an internal AI tool to pivot to wallet engineers and obtain signing access.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion stolen across 11 cryptocurrencies — the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. Binance recovered about $2.8 billion in frozen stablecoins, leaving about $3.25 billion in unrecoverable holdings. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korean state hackers.

incidents.victim: US Department of Homeland Security (DHS), including ICE, CBP, USCIS, CISA
incidents.vector: Hacktivists claim the data came from a DHS Okta-based identity system; Okta disputes it was breached and DHS has not confirmed the method.
incidents.impact: Personal and organizational data on roughly 41,000 DHS employees and contractors was published via a transparency site, including names, work contacts, reporting structures, and references to surveillance and undercover-operations programs.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government IT systems and began extracting data before being detected by IT staff.
incidents.impact: Data on roughly one-third of Moldova's population was stolen; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime, and shipping companies
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ransomware and data extortion
incidents.vector: Compromise of maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec was used as a supply-chain pivot into downstream port authority and shipping company customers.
incidents.impact: Ransomware group n0n listed 40+ victims on its dark web leak site; the payment deadline expired Oct 19.

incidents.victim: Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs
incidents.vector: Breach of the ministry's internal network; the secure segment was reportedly not impacted.
incidents.impact: Data on 3,600 employees, including names and email addresses, was stolen.

incidents.victim: DigiCert business customers
incidents.vector: An internal business system was inadvertently left externally accessible after a network migration, allowing an unassigned account to be created.
incidents.impact: Customer names, business emails, phone numbers, and identity documents (driver's licenses, passports, utility bills) were exposed; certificate-issuance capability and login credentials were not affected.
